vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: feishu-doc-collab
Version: 1.1.0

The skill performs highly intrusive system modifications by patching the OpenClaw Feishu extension's source code (monitor.ts) to intercept document edit events. It reads sensitive configuration data, including authentication tokens, from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to trigger agent sessions via local HTTP POST requests to the gateway. While these actions are aligned with the stated goal of real-time Feishu collaboration, the method of implementation (source code patching) and the reliance on a protocol that processes user-controlled document content create a significant surface for indirect prompt injection. No evidence of intentional malice or data exfiltration was found, but the high-privilege file modifications warrant a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill does what it says (adds real‑time AI replies to Feishu docs) but it patches OpenClaw's core Feishu monitor, reads your local OpenClaw config (which can contain secrets), and injects code that triggers a local agent endpoint — actions that are powerful and deserve caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description match its behavior: it patches the Feishu monitor to trigger agent sessions on document edits and implements an in‑doc chat protocol and optional Bitable integration. Requesting access to Feishu events and using the OpenClaw hooks endpoint is coherent for this purpose. However, the implementation requires modifying core extension code under /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/extensions/feishu/, which is a higher‑privilege action than many skills and should be expected and accepted explicitly by the operator.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions (and the injected code) read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to obtain hooks.token and gateway.port, append to /tmp/feishu-events.log, and POST a structured agent message to http://127.0.0.1:{port}/hooks/agent instructing the agent to read and append document content. Those operations go beyond just calling Feishu APIs: they (a) modify core extension behavior, (b) access local config files that may contain other credentials, and (c) instruct the local agent with detailed commands — all of which increase risk and deserve explicit consent and review.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no packaged install; instead the included patch script (scripts/patch-monitor.sh) edits monitor.ts in the system OpenClaw installation and writes a backup. While the script is idempotent and local (no external downloads), modifying system-installed runtime files is inherently risky: mistakes can break updates, introduce persistence, or be used to change agent behavior globally.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, but both SKILL.md and the injected code read ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for hooks.token and gateway.port (and implicitly rely on Feishu channel credentials configured there). That file may contain app secrets and other credentials. The skill does not clearly declare or limit what it will read from that config, so requested access is under‑declared and therefore disproportionate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true, but it modifies another extension's source (monitor.ts) — changing system behavior and installing a trigger that invokes the agent whenever Feishu emits edits. This effectively grants ongoing privileged behavior (modifying event handling across the Feishu integration) and should be treated as a privileged change to the platform, requiring code review and stricter operational controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing:

- This skill modifies OpenClaw's Feishu monitor.ts (a core extension file). Back up /usr/lib/node_modules/openclaw/extensions/feishu/src/monitor.ts and test in a non-production environment first.
- The injected code reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to obtain hooks.token and gateway.port. That config can contain Feishu app secrets and other credentials — review the file and be comfortable with the skill reading it.
- The patch triggers the local /hooks/agent endpoint by sending an instruction payload that causes the agent to read and append document content. Verify how /hooks/agent authenticates and what the agent is allowed to do; a compromised or overly-privileged agent could be misused to exfiltrate data.
- The script is local (no remote download), but still alters system files. If OpenClaw updates, you must re-apply or maintain the patch; consider the operational burden and the risk of upgrade breakage.
- If you decide to proceed: inspect the patch code carefully (the hooks injection is visible in scripts/patch-monitor.sh and references/monitor-full-patched.ts), configure a dedicated hooks token with minimal scope, restrict network and agent privileges where possible, keep logs/monitoring enabled, and run the skill first in a sandbox/org where a misconfiguration won't expose sensitive data.

If you are not comfortable with core file patches or the skill reading local configuration containing secrets, do not install it or obtain a vetted, packaged integration from a trusted source.
